- A single line labelled "prefix amortization" for 3,600 tokens.

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear callout and for attaching the invoice. Looping in Camila (CS lead) and Karthik (pricing) to make sure I cover the billing and technical sides.

Short answer: there wasn't a surprise surcharge — what you're seeing is the interplay of three billing levers we apply for short-lived calls: per-call minimums (microfloor), prefix/KV amortization for model context warm-up, and invoice-line compaction for small items. I'll walk through a concise worked example below.

Worked example (based on your 12 short calls):
- Each of the 12 calls used ~40 tokens request + 6 tokens response = ~46 tokens actual.
- Microfloor = 500 tokens per call (policy for very short inference requests to cover scheduling/kernel overhead). So naive charge = 12 * 500 = 6,000 tokens.
- Prefix amortization: when a conversation or batch triggers a model context prefetch (e.g., embeddings/prefixs) we amortize that cost across the group of calls within a configured amortization window. In August your tenant had a prefix prefetch of 3,600 tokens that we amortized across the day's calls.
- Invoice compaction: to reduce many small lines, our invoicing pipeline sometimes emits a combined amortization line instead of repeating identical microfloor items; that can look like a separate residual.

Net view: the 3,600-token prefix is not an extra per-call tax — it's the baseline context load split across the day's active calls. If we spread that prefix across the 12 calls, that's 300 tokens per call additional amortized cost (3,600 / 12). So effective billed tokens per call = 500 (microfloor) + 300 (amortized prefix) = 800 tokens.

We recognize this can be surprising. Options we can offer:
1) Adjust amortization window (longer window => prefix amortized across more calls, lowers per-call share).
2) Apply microfloor exemptions for certain API keys if you can route many tiny calls through a batching gateway (reduces scheduling overhead).
3) Convert the tenant to a small reserved pool for predictable throughput (removes microfloor economics).

I'll attach a worked spreadsheet with the per-call breakdown and a sample invoice mapping. Camila/Karthik — any additional detail to add on the compaction/invoice formatting?

Best,
Sergio

Hi Maya — quick follow-up on the formal rules so your AP team has something they can reconcile against the invoice:

Policy summary (effective for your tenant unless we agree an exception):
1) Microfloor (per-call minimum) applies to inference requests below the microfloor token threshold; current microfloor = 500 tokens/call. This covers scheduling/kernel overhead and short-lived model init.
2) Prefix amortization: one-time context warm-up cost is attributed to the first request that triggered it and then amortized across subsequent requests that occur within the configured amortization window for that tenant/day. The amortization amount appears as a single "prefix amortization" line when compacting invoice entries.
3) Rounding & invoice compaction: token charges are computed per-call then rounded to integer tokens; we perform line-level compaction for readability. Invoice rounding does not increase aggregate token consumption.

If you need a formal one-page note for AP we'll produce an "invoice guide" that maps invoice lines to the above rules and includes the worked example from Sergio/Camila.

Action items:
- Maya: confirm whether you'd like the amortization window extended and whether you prefer separate line items for microfloor vs amortization (some customers prefer granular lines; others prefer compacted lines).
- Sergio/Camila: I'll route a draft invoice-guide and the 3-month forecast once Maya confirms scope.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if that helps with AP reconciliation.

Karthik Iyer | Pricing Lead, Redwood Inference
